why: Neither short is a practical fade of an overreaction or a practical expression of a sustained growth shock on this frozen packet. AUDJPY's 2026-11-05 ECB reference move was a -0.078% log change, split into AUDUSD -0.208% log and USDJPY +0.130% log, so the yen weakened on the same fixing as the NASDAQ -5.68% log drop. The five-year richness screen cannot be rebuilt from 126 observations, and inside those observations the cross sits in the lower part of its own range. Japan's AI-credit exposure and the same-day oil rebound are live reasons for the cross to rise. AUDNZD is high on its screens and high inside the 126 prints, but the 2026-10-28 jump was a NZDUSD drop, NZDUSD's cheap screen is that same fact, AU-NZ and NZ-US yield histories are empty, and the relationship AUDNZD~AU-NZ_2Y is insufficient, so there is no rates fair value. NZ inflation and labor components are calendar_unparsed with the previous release retained at 2026-Q2. Both dollars fell together on 2026-11-05 and the cross rose. Loss budgets are zero.
percentile_fade_versus_fundamental: A percentile is a screen. The pairs-screen pctile_5y and z_5y fields are quoted only with the caveat that the 126-day history cannot recompute them. AUDJPY pctile_1y 47.02 and z_1y 0.19 are a mid one-year screen; pctile_5y 89.40 and z_5y 1.67 are a rich five-year screen that this sample does not rebuild. Of the 126 AUDJPY observations, 33 are at or below the 2026-11-05 print, so the available history places the cross low, which is the wrong location for a fade of upside overreaction. There was no upside overreaction on the shock day. AUDNZD pctile_1y 97.02, pctile_5y 99.40, z_1y 1.52, and z_5y 2.75 line up with a high location inside the 126 prints (119 of 126 at or below the last print; sample high 1.2528742893240683 on 2026-10-28). That location is not a separate fundamental. The 2026-10-28 log move was AUDNZD +1.591% against NZDUSD -1.580% and AUDUSD +0.012%. NZDUSD pctile_5y 3.37 and z_5y -1.44 are the cheap-kiwi screen and are not independent proof of the short. Domestic scores that exist point at a cooler, staler New Zealand: NZ activity impulse -16.88 versus AU activity impulse +2.23, both reference 2026-08, and NZ labor temperature cool at 36.51 versus AU labor neutral at 45.74. NZ's scored inflation and labor rows are calendar_unparsed and previous-release-retained at 2026-Q2, so they are not a fresh relative surprise. AU inflation is warm at 67.25 on a 2026-09 reference and NZ inflation is warm at 64.25 on 2026-Q2. Empty AU-NZ yield histories kill a rates-spread fair value. The high cross can be the relative price of that growth gap. Fading the percentile would take the other side of the only relative growth evidence in the packet.
japan_ai_and_oil_countercase: The countercase stands on the news and the oil prints, whether AUDJPY sold off or not. It did not sell off. news:5dd4b0f051ae8ece (Reuters, 2026-11-05T20:15:00-05:00) says SoftBank shares dropped 11% on Friday and the cost of insuring its debt hit a four-year high as AI-profitability worries roiled markets. news:5280c2a7f410b0c3 (Bloomberg, 2026-11-05T11:00:00-05:00) says SoftBank led declines in Asian dollar bonds as the AI stock rout extended into credit. news:80f84c85f21e0aa9 (CNBC, 2026-11-06T05:24:52-05:00, headline only) records growing AI-debt concern around a reported sale of data-center loans. A short AUDJPY is long yen against Australia. Japan is inside this AI-credit complex, and the 2026-11-05 fixing already showed a weaker yen (USDJPY log +0.130%) while JGBs rallied (JP_2Y 189.1 to 186.0, -3.1 bp; JP_10Y 285.5 to 280.6, -4.9 bp). Bond strength without yen strength leaves the safe-haven leg unconfirmed. Oil rebounded the same day: WTI 88.12000274658203 to 90.5199966430664, log +2.687%; Brent 94.62000274658203 to 98.29000091552734, log +3.805%. Japan imports oil and Australia's terms of trade take the other side, so a rebound pushes AUDJPY up and hurts the short. The larger WTI and Brent down-jumps on 2026-11-02 and 2026-11-04 sit in futures histories whose note says contract rolls can distort screens; those jumps are not treated here as clean economic returns. The recorded 5 Nov rebound is enough to keep the importer burden on the table.

declined_reason: AUDJPY did not reprice the 5 Nov equity drop, the yen weakened, oil rebounded, and Japan is inside the AI-credit story, so the short is neither a fade of an overreaction nor a clean growth-shock expression. AUDNZD's high screen is the cheap kiwi seen again, the domestic evidence that exists is stale on the NZ side and leans toward NZ softness, and there is no AU-NZ yield history from which to build a fair value. Both dollars moved together. No loss budget is accepted on either path.
objections: AUDNZD is high inside the 126 observations themselves, not only on a five-year screen the sample cannot rebuild. Refusing the short gives up a possible further giveback from a location that is already extreme in this window. That cost is real and is still not a thesis.

One fixing cannot prove AUDJPY is immune to a sustained risk shock. A later Australian-dollar decline with a stable or stronger yen would falsify the no-trade. The same packet's weaker yen, oil rebound, and SoftBank credit stress are why that later path is not funded now.

Three submitted lead actions open an AUDNZD short. They are not fills and not a crowding measure. Their shared evidence is the five-year percentile and the cheap NZDUSD screen, which this node does not treat as independent confirmation.
